audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was scored Kennen though its why says never commit; levels 2 and 3 were scored Skill and Tryndamere though both whys describe Kennen chunking and stunning him; first item was scored Tryndamere though its why ends 'genuinely even here'.
audit.why: 46.77% over 201 games — a losing lane, but one where Kennen genuinely owns levels 2-3 and 6 before crit items arrive.

audit.why: Kennen's spikes are 2-3 and level 6; Tryndamere's are 4-5 on Spinning Slash and the crit-item window. Undying Rage at 120/100/80 means the rank-1 gap between ults is a full two minutes.
audit.corrected: 120s at rank 1 and Spinning Slash's 12/11/10/9/8 written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is described as a plain slow in four fields, and the level-6 text claims the storm means 'he can't simply spin out'.
audit.why: Mocking Shout reduces the attack damage of surrounding champions, and only slows enemies whose BACKS are turned to him — so it punishes fleeing and does nothing to a Kennen who turns and fights. And Spinning Slash is 650 range against Slicing Maelstrom's 550 radius, so he out-ranges the storm and can leave it; the reason the ult still wins is the burn continuing while Undying Rage expires, not an inability to escape.
audit.corrected: The back-turned condition stated in whys[3], spikes[2] and mid; the level-6 claim re-grounded on timing the burst to the end of his immunity.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bloodlust is never named and the healing is attributed to his crits.
audit.why: Bloodlust is the Q: it consumes Fury to heal him on a 12s cooldown, and his attack damage rises as he drops lower. That is what Grievous Wounds shuts off, and it is why bursting him to low health without anti-heal is worse than not damaging him at all.
audit.corrected: Named in dosFull[1].t, dontsFull[1].d and late, with the 12s cooldown attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage was tracked as 'unkillable 5s' with no cooldown.
audit.why: 120/100/80 is the number that decides whether you may commit at all: at rank 1 you get two full minutes of window between his immunities, at rank 3 only 80 seconds.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his, not yours: his E gap-close plus W slow lets him stick on your squishy body the second your mark stun goes on cooldown, and his Fury-stacked crits now hurt. Respect that window and chip from range. Then at 6 you reclaim the lane — Slicing Maelstrom plus a Q-W-E mark chain stun-locks him through his spin, and because the storm keeps ticking he can't simply spin out. Hold Flash for the R all-in and you win that one duel cleanly, even into his Undying Rage if you time the burst as it expires.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his, not yours: Spinning Slash closes 650 the second your mark stun goes on cooldown and his Fury-stacked crits now hurt, so chip from range — and remember Mocking Shout only slows you while your back is turned. Then at 6 you reclaim the lane: Slicing Maelstrom plus a Q-W-E mark chain stun-locks him, and the storm keeps burning while Undying Rage ticks away. Hold Flash for the R all-in and time your burst for the moment his immunity ends — that duel is yours cleanly while his crit items are still unfinished.

edits.before: This is where it slips. Once his crit items and Fury are online he tanks your entire R combo, drops to 1 HP under Undying Rage for five seconds, and then spins you to death — your squishy caster body can't survive his sustained DPS once your stun chain is on cooldown. You cannot out-duel a fed Tryndamere in the sidelane, so stop trying. Pivot to grouping: your AoE R and global threat make you a teamfight engager, and that's where you cash a lead a 1v1 will never give you against him.
edits.after: This is where it slips. Once his crit items and Fury are online he tanks your entire R combo, survives on Undying Rage, then Bloodlust heals the whole thing back on a 12-second cooldown and he spins you down — and without Grievous Wounds your squishy caster body cannot out-damage that. You will not out-duel a fed Tryndamere in the sidelane, so stop trying. Pivot to grouping: your AoE R and global threat make you a teamfight engager, and that is where you cash a lead.

edits.before: Build Fury so his autos crit, then E-in and W-slow to stick on your fragile body
edits.after: Build Battle Fury for crits, then Spinning Slash in and Mocking Shout your retreat

notes: Two real mechanics were missing. Mocking Shout reduces attack damage on everyone around him and only slows enemies whose BACKS are turned — so the instruction 'kite out' was quietly telling the reader to take the slow; turning to fight removes it. And Spinning Slash is 650 range against Slicing Maelstrom's 550 radius, so the old claim that the storm stops him spinning out is false; what actually wins the level-6 fight is timing the burn so it is still ticking when Undying Rage expires and leaves him at 1 HP. Bloodlust (Q, 12s) was never named even though the page tells you to buy anti-heal. packet.suspectNames flags 'Build Fury' in wants.foe[0] as a probable wrong name for Battle Fury — half right: the passive is Battle Fury and the resource is Fury, so I used the full name in the rewrite. One thing I did NOT touch: the existing 'five seconds' duration on Undying Rage. Riot's text in the kit file gives no duration, so I left the claim alone rather than assert or delete it.
